courses.summary: MBBS is the Students Traffic catalogue category for undergraduate-entry medicine degrees. University of Nicosia maps its 6-Year MD (Nicosia) programme to this category: a direct-entry, single-cycle six-year programme leading to the Doctor of Medicine (MD) qualification. This does not cover the university's separate 5-year graduate-entry MD pathway.

universities.name: University of Nicosia
universities.summary: University of Nicosia opened the first medical school in Cyprus in 2011 and runs a direct-entry, six-year Doctor of Medicine programme in Nicosia (360 ECTS), alongside a separate graduate-entry pathway and an Athens campus not covered by this record. Cyprus's national accreditation registry certifies this programme from Winter 2025-2026 through Spring 2030, and EU Directive 2005/36/EC names the university as an approved medical-degree awarding body.
universities.campusLifestyle: University of Nicosia Medical School has graduated a large alumni cohort now practising at several hundred medical centres worldwide, and maintains a dedicated USMLE Study Club and individualized career-advising structure from Year 1, reflecting a strong institutional focus on the US residency pathway. Students who remain in Cyprus for clinical training receive free Greek-language lessons to support patient communication.
universities.cityProfile: Nicosia is Cyprus's capital. The university operates its own on-campus UNIC Medical Centre, described as the first of its kind in Cyprus, operating under the Cyprus General Healthcare System and serving as a primary-care training ground for students.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS MD programme begins longitudinal, primary-care-focused clinical placements from Year 2, increases clinical intensity through Years 3-4 (including a Year 4 transition rotation across Primary Care, General Surgery and Internal Medicine plus a research project), and moves to an almost entirely clinical structure in Years 5-6, with rotating sub-specialty placements (cardiology, respiratory, gastroenterology, nephrology/urology, paediatrics, obstetrics/gynaecology, psychiatry, neurology and more) culminating in a 6-week clinical elective that can be taken abroad. The university does not publish specific named teaching-hospital partners, describing clinical sites only generically as 'affiliated hospitals' whose sub-rotation sequence depends on clinical capacity; students may also opt into international clinical-training placements in the UK, USA, Switzerland or Germany at additional cost. Graduates receive the MD degree.
universities.hostelOverview: The university offers three residence complexes near the Medical School -- SIX (314 rooms), Triangle (147 rooms) and U (399 single-occupancy studios with an option to share) -- bookable through the same account used for the admissions application. No official per-month or per-year accommodation cost is published; applicants should confirm current rates directly with the university. Private studios, flats and houses around campus are also available, and the university arranges short-term accommodation (from budget options to hotels) for the arrival period before permanent housing begins.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published. The university's own minimum living-cost estimate for Nicosia is EUR 12,000 per year, which should be planned alongside tuition and accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. The university's Student Services team assists with housing and settling-in support for incoming students.
universities.studentSupport: Every student is assigned a personal tutor from Year 1, alongside one-on-one Career Adviser meetings, an individualized career profile for postgraduate planning, and alumni-led mentoring. A dedicated USMLE Study Club supports students targeting US residency pathways.
whyChoose: The first medical school in Cyprus (founded 2011), with a 6-Year MD (Nicosia) programme certified by Cyprus's national accreditation registry from Winter 2025-2026 through Spring 2030.

EU Directive 2005/36/EC names University of Nicosia explicitly as an approved awarding body for the automatically-recognized Cypriot medical qualification, effective for degrees awarded from October 2014 onward.

A strong, institutionally-supported US residency pathway: since 2024 ECFMG certifies only WFME-accredited-programme graduates, and the university's CYQAA/DIPAE accreditation carries WFME Recognition Status, with a dedicated USMLE Study Club and individualized career advising.
A need-based scholarship of up to 20% of tuition, available to admitted students after receiving an offer.
A fully refundable seat-reservation deposit if an admitted student ultimately decides not to enroll.
thingsToConsider: University of Nicosia also runs a separate 5-year graduate-entry MD pathway (bachelor's-degree holders only, EUR 25,000/year, 300 ECTS, accredited only through Spring 2027) and a 6-Year MD at an Athens, Greece campus -- this record covers the direct-entry 6-Year MD in Nicosia specifically, not those other pathways.

The university does not publish a fixed 2026/27 application deadline; admissions are presented as rolling ('Admissions Open'), with a September intake -- confirm current-cycle deadlines directly with the admissions team.
Choosing an international clinical-training placement in years 5-6 adds a substantial supplement: EUR 6,000/year for UK/USA placements or EUR 3,000/year for Switzerland/Germany placements.
No specific named teaching hospitals are published for the Cyprus-based clinical placements; the university describes sites only generically as 'affiliated hospitals.'
Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission NEET-UG Eligibility Certificate requirement; this is not referenced or administered by the university.
bestFitFor: Students with strong secondary-school grades (roughly 90% average, A-Level ABB, or IB 32) targeting a US residency pathway, given the university's dedicated USMLE support structure.
Applicants comfortable with rolling admissions and confirming exact deadlines directly with the university rather than relying on a fixed published date.
Families able to budget for substantial optional clinical-placement supplements if targeting a UK, USA, Switzerland or Germany elective.

faq.question: Is the 6-Year MD programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Admission follows completion of secondary education, with no separate bachelor's stage required first. This is different from University of Nicosia's separate 5-year Graduate-Entry MD, which requires an existing bachelor's degree.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the MD (Doctor of Medicine), a Cypriot medical qualification listed under EU Directive 2005/36/EC Annex V for automatic recognition across the EU/EEA, with University of Nicosia named explicitly as an approved awarding body for degrees from October 2014 onward.

faq.question: What entrance requirements does the university use?
faq.answer: Admission is grade-based (roughly a 90% secondary-school average, A-Level ABB, or IB 32 overall including Biology plus one of Chemistry/Physics/Mathematics), plus English proficiency and a mandatory online interview -- there is no separate written entrance exam for this direct-entry pathway.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 24,000 per year for the 6-Year MD in Nicosia. The university's separate 5-year Graduate-Entry MD is priced differently, at EUR 25,000 per year.

faq.question: Are there additional fees besides tuition?
faq.answer: Yes -- a EUR 60 non-refundable application fee, a EUR 1,500 administrative fee and a EUR 3,500 seat-reservation deposit (both deducted from first-semester tuition, with the deposit fully refundable if the student does not enroll), plus visa, insurance and malpractice-cover fees for non-EU students.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The academic year starts in September. The university presents admissions as rolling ('Admissions Open') rather than tied to one fixed deadline -- confirm the current application timeline directly with the admissions team.

faq.question: Is a scholarship available for international Medicine students?
faq.answer: Yes -- a need-based scholarship of up to 20% of tuition is available, but only after an applicant has met admissions requirements, completed the interview and received an offer; the offer letter specifies the scholarship application deadline.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

fee.notes: Officially published 2026/27 tuition for the 6-Year MD (Nicosia): EUR 24,000/year, per the university's official Financial Information page. Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum. Additional confirmed one-off/annual fees: EUR 60 application fee (non-refundable), EUR 1,500 administrative fee and EUR 3,500 seat-reservation deposit (both deducted from first-semester tuition, deposit fully refundable if the student does not enroll), plus visa, insurance and malpractice-cover fees for non-EU students. Choosing an international clinical-training placement in years 5-6 adds EUR 6,000/year (UK/USA) or EUR 3,000/year (Switzerland/Germany). The university's separate 5-year Graduate-Entry MD is priced at EUR 25,000/year and is not covered by this record.
